gold_spans.quote: Also Hipparchus invented his own Hipparchic calendar cycle as an improvement upon the Callippic cycle.

Hipparchus dropped one more day from four Callippic cycles (304 years), creating the Hipparchic cycle with an average year of 365+1/4−1/304 or 365.24671 days, which was close to his tropical year of 365+1/4−1/300 or 365.24667 days.

known_distractor_spans.why: The 76-year Callippic cycle and the 19-year Metonic cycle are both given in the same paragraph as the question's premise.
The same sentence carries 365.24671 and 365.24667 days, two figures a reader may return instead of the cycle length.

provenance.author: sj157
provenance.notes: Hipparchus is the join key and appears in neither question nor answer; the two spans are 643k characters apart.

answers.question: How many more synodic months does one Callippic cycle contain than one exeligmos?

gold_spans.quote: 940 synodic months

The exeligmos is 669 synodic months (every eclipse cycle must be an integer number of synodic months), almost exactly 726 draconic months (which ensures the sun and moon are in alignment during the new moon), and also almost exactly 717 anomalistic months (ensuring the moon is at the same point of its elliptic orbit).

known_distractor_spans.why: The Metonic cycle is defined as 235 synodic months, the third synodic-month count in the dossier and the likeliest wrong operand.
The saros is 223 synodic months, a fourth count of the same kind.
A large table lists synodic-month counts for dozens of cycles at once, so a single retrieved chunk can supply many wrong operands.

provenance.author: sj157
provenance.notes: Derived: 940 - 669 = 271, over two pages that sit 2.7k characters apart but describe different cycles.
